requirements.requirement: On node1, a web service uses TCP port 8081 and is reachable through the loopback interface.
requirements.summary: Before and after restart, the service was active, listened exclusively on 127.0.0.1:8081, and returned the expected HTTP page through 127.0.0.1.

requirements.requirement: The TCP 8081 service is not reachable through node1's external interfaces.
requirements.summary: Node1's external IPv4 address was 10.100.55.10. Direct probes to 10.100.55.10:8081 were refused before and after restart, while socket inventories showed only a 127.0.0.1:8081 listener.

overall_summary: Both public-task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide node-restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the post-restart identity differed, and the enabled service, content, listener binding, and external isolation all recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: External-address probes originated on node1 rather than a separate host, although the exclusive 127.0.0.1 socket binding directly corroborates the isolation result.
Two probe-output files were not cleaned from /tmp; this affects hygiene rather than service functionality.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: creating the web content, defining and enabling the service, and performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting or security-weakening mutation was found. The only avoidable retained residue was two small probe-output files created by cmd-4a05cd74c6604bcc and cmd-9a07574422034a53; both remained under /tmp after completion. No failed services or package-health damage was observed.
